bullets: How to sketch straight lines from gradient and intercept, read graphs, spot parallel lines, and sketch a quadratic from its roots and turning point
slides.heading: E-Math functions and graphs: straight lines and quadratics
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we sketch straight lines from gradient and intercept, read values off a graph, spot parallel lines, sketch a quadratic, and finish by untangling steepness from intercept.

bullets: Sketch y = mx + c from its gradient and intercept and read a gradient and intercept off a graph
Recognise parallel lines and sketch a quadratic from its roots and turning point
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these things.

bullets: Two lines cross the y-axis at very different heights - which one is steeper?
Does starting higher mean climbing faster?
slides.heading: Which line climbs fastest?
slides.notes: Ask for a show of hands and take two or three answers without judging them yet; say: the scenes will give us a way to settle it by measuring, not by guessing from height.

bullets: In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept where x = 0
Parallel lines share the same gradient; a quadratic is set by its roots and its turning point
slides.heading: Gradient, intercept, roots and turning point
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the map for the whole lesson: gradient tells you the climb, intercept tells you the start, and roots plus turning point fix a curve.

bullets: Plot the intercept (0, −3) first, then step run 1 and rise 2
Join the points: the gradient is 2 and the intercept is −3
slides.heading: Sketch y = 2x − 3 from gradient and intercept
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: watch the pen mark the intercept below the origin, step out one right and two up, then join the points into the finished line.

bullets: The line crosses the y-axis at (0, 2), so the intercept is 2
From (0, 2) to (4, 8) the rise is 6 over a run of 4, so the gradient is 3/2
slides.heading: Read the gradient and the intercept off a graph
slides.notes: Follow the reading point as it moves: count the run first, then the rise, and divide rise by run to get the gradient.

bullets: y = 3x + 1 and y = 3x − 4 both have gradient 3
Different intercepts, same climb: the lines never meet
slides.heading: Parallel lines share a gradient
slides.notes: Watch both lines grow side by side at exactly the same steepness: same gradient with different starting heights means parallel.

bullets: Setting y = 0 gives x² − 4 = 0, so the roots are x = −2 and x = 2
The turning point (0, −4) is the minimum of the curve
slides.heading: Roots and the turning point of y = x² − 4
slides.notes: Follow the tracer along the curve: mark where it crosses the x-axis for the roots, then find the lowest point for the turning point.

bullets: Line A y = 4x − 6 has gradient 4; line B y = x + 3 has gradient 1
A starts lower but climbs faster: steepness comes from the gradient
slides.heading: A common mistake: the bigger intercept is steeper
slides.notes: Name the mix-up out loud before anyone settles on it: starting height and climbing rate are two different things, and only the gradient measures the climb.

bullets: Intercept −3: plot (0, −3), then use gradient 2 to plot (1, −1) and (2, 1)
Join the points with a straight line and label it y = 2x − 3
slides.heading: Worked example: sketching y = 2x − 3
slides.notes: Talk through it slowly: intercept first, then repeated rise-over-run steps, then join and label the line.

bullets: Sketch y = 3x + 1, then read the gradient and intercept off a given graph
State the roots and turning point of y = x² − 9 and say which of two lines is steeper
slides.heading: Your turn: sketch, read and compare
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each part: press them to name the intercept, the rise over run, and the gradient they compared.

bullets: On your own: one sketching question, one reading-a-graph question, one quadratic question
Watch the comparison question: compare gradients, not starting heights
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for the intercept plotted first, rise over run for the gradient, and roots plus turning point on the quadratic.
